title: Lamphun 1-Day Itinerary: Hariphunchai, Old Town & Cafes | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: An easy one-day Lamphun itinerary in northern Thailand: pay respects at Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, walk the walled old town, see Wat Chamthewi (Ku Kut) and the Hariphunchai museum, then unwind at a cafe — with real opening hours and a route that doesn't double back.

h1:
Lamphun 1-Day Itinerary
Hariphunchai Temple, Old Town & Cafes
intro: Lamphun is a small town you can comfortably see in a single day. Almost all the highlights are within walking distance inside the old city walls. Start the morning at Wat Phra That Hariphunchai in the center of town, swing by the Hariphunchai museum and Wat Chamthewi mid-morning, eat northern Thai food at lunch, hide from the afternoon sun at a cafe, and finish with a stroll along the Kuang River at dusk. This is a plan you can actually follow, with opening hours we've checked.

blocks.html: The best thing about Lamphun is how small and compact it is. The old town sits inside conch-shell-shaped walls beside the Kuang River, and Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, the Hariphunchai museum, and the market are all within walking distance of each other. The only outlier is Wat Chamthewi (Ku Kut), about 1.5 km west of the walls — a quick drive or bike ride away. The trick is to start at the temple early, when it's still cool and quiet, then work through the other spots in town in order so you never have to backtrack.

blocks.title: Before you set out
blocks.html: Lamphun is only about 26 km from Chiang Mai, so many people drive or take the train over for a morning-to-evening day trip. You can walk to nearly everything in town, but to reach Wat Chamthewi easily, rent a motorbike for around 250–300 THB a day or grab a local ride. Some guesthouses also lend out bicycles for free.

blocks.text: Morning — Pay respects at Wat Phra That Hariphunchai

blocks.html: Start the day at Lamphun's main landmark. Wat Phra That Hariphunchai sits in the heart of the old town. It's a royal temple and home to the golden Lanna-style chedi that northern Thais hold in deep reverence. Inside the grounds you'll find the Khong gateway arch, a scripture hall, a drum tower, and old Buddha images to wander past quietly. In the early light, the low sun hitting the golden chedi looks beautiful — and there are far fewer people than later in the morning.

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.title: Inside the walls · Wat Phra That Hariphunchai

items.activity: Grab a simple breakfast near the temple — khao ngiao, khao soi, or coffee with patongko
items.note: Shops around the old town open early with friendly prices. Fuel up before the temple walk.

items.activity: Enter Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, pay respects at the golden chedi, and walk through the main viharn and the various halls
items.note: Open roughly 06:00–21:00, free entry · Mornings have lovely light and few people. Dress modestly and remove your shoes before entering the viharn.

items.activity: Walk around the temple courtyard and photograph the Khong gateway arch and the pair of guardian lions out front
items.note: The courtyard in front of the chedi is Lamphun's classic photo spot, easy to shoot in the morning.

items.activity: Walk across the road to the Hariphunchai National Museum, diagonally opposite the temple
items.note: Just a few minutes on foot — no need to drive.

items.label: Day trips from Lamphun
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: Mid-morning — Hariphunchai Museum and Wat Chamthewi

blocks.html: Lamphun was once the kingdom of Hariphunchai, founded by Queen Chamthewi more than 1,300 years ago. If you want to understand where the town came from, the Hariphunchai National Museum lays the groundwork well — it gathers Buddha images, stone inscriptions, and artifacts from the Hariphunchai–Lanna era. After that, head outside the walls to Wat Chamthewi (Ku Kut), home to a rare stepped, square-tiered chedi seldom seen in the north.

items.activity: Walk through the Hariphunchai National Museum
items.note: Open roughly 09:00–16:00, closed Monday–Tuesday and public holidays · Entry around 30 THB for Thai visitors · If you come early in the week, skip ahead to another stop instead.

items.activity: Drive or cycle about 1.5 km outside the walls to Wat Chamthewi (Ku Kut)
items.note: See the Suwan Chang Kot and Ratana chedis, true Hariphunchai architecture. Free entry.

items.activity: Drive back into town to find somewhere for lunch
items.note: Before the sun gets harsh and the restaurants fill up.

blocks.title: If you come on a Monday or Tuesday
blocks.html: The Hariphunchai museum is closed Monday–Tuesday. If you arrive on those days, spend a bit longer walking the temple grounds, then carry on to Wat Chamthewi and the town market instead. It won't throw off the overall plan much.

blocks.text: Lunch — Northern Thai food and Lamphun bites

blocks.html: Lamphun is an easy place to eat. The local specialties are northern Thai home-style dishes like khanom jeen nam ngiao, khao soi, and kaeng hang le, plus the unusual pork-and-longan noodle soup (Lamphun is longan country). Most shops are in town and around the Wiang Yong area. Pick one to refuel before the afternoon.

items.name: Khao Soi Ban Yong
items.blurb: A northern Thai spot in the Wiang Yong area that Lamphun locals recommend. The standout is the loaded khao soi, with khanom jeen nam ngiao, yen ta fo, noodles, and clear noodle soup also on the menu. Relaxed, homey atmosphere.

items.name: Pork & Longan Noodle Soup
items.blurb: The town's quirky signature in longan country: broth simmered with pork bones and dried longan for a rounded, sweet-fragrant flavor, with tender stewed pork and noodles with just the right chew. Hard to find anywhere else.

items.name: Khanom Sen Mor Din
items.blurb: An old wooden house in a garden-home style around the Pa Sak area. The standouts are khanom jeen nam ngiao, the coconut-milk nam ya, and green chicken curry. Shady and pleasant for a relaxed meal.

items.name: Heuan Lamphun
items.blurb: A northern Thai restaurant in a wooden-house setting serving local northern dishes like nam phrik ong, kaeng hang le, and sai ua. Best as a main meal where you order several plates to share.

items.name: Yen Ta Fo Je Mam
items.blurb: An in-town yen ta fo shop that stays busy. It comes fully loaded with squid, meatballs, pork blood, and tofu in a rich broth, and stays open late — good for a lighter meal.

blocks.text: Afternoon — Walk the old town and pause at a cafe

blocks.html: The afternoon is when Lamphun's old town is at its best for walking. The sun softens, the streets inside the walls go quiet, and there are old wooden houses, ancient city walls, and small shops to amble past. When your legs tire, find a cafe to rest. Lamphun has plenty in town, from rooftop spots with town views to renovated old houses, with coffee in the 55–90 THB range, about standard for an upcountry cafe.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.title: In the old town · walk + cafe

items.activity: Stroll inside the old city walls, taking in wooden houses, ancient walls, and the city gate arches
items.note: Everything inside the walls is walkable. Shoot some street photos to capture the small-town feel.

items.activity: Stop at a cafe for coffee and a sweet, out of the afternoon sun
items.note: Pick from the cafe list below — both rooftop spots with town views and old houses.

items.activity: Shop for souvenirs — woven cotton, dried longan, and longan products
items.note: Lamphun is known for its weaving and longan, sold at shops in town and at the market.

blocks.text: Cafes in Lamphun town to drop by during the day

blocks.html: Pick one of these for an afternoon break. They're all in town or the old quarter, within walking distance or a short drive. Opening hours can change, so check the shop's page before you go to be sure.

items.name: Yann Slow Bar Cafe
items.blurb: A rooftop slow-bar cafe in the center of town with a classic vintage feel. The highlight is the angle that takes in the Lamphun cityscape and the chedi — a chill spot for an afternoon coffee.

items.name: Aq Bur Old Town
items.blurb: An old-town cafe in the center, just past the governor's residence before the post office, across from a Punthai Coffee. Open from morning through evening, so it works for both daytime and dusk.

items.name: willwhy.house
items.blurb: A house cafe in the old quarter near Nong Dok. The shop is a home, so it feels warm and welcoming — good for sitting quietly and resting your legs after sightseeing.

blocks.text: Evening — A stroll along the Kuang River and dinner

blocks.html: Close out the day with the easy mood along the Kuang River, which runs parallel to the eastern city wall. The evening breeze makes for a pleasant walk, and if you happen to catch an evening market or walking street, there's plenty to graze on. After that, find dinner in town before heading back to your stay or returning to Chiang Mai.

items.activity: Stroll along the Kuang River, watching the late-afternoon sun and the eastern city wall
items.note: A cool breeze and a quiet spot where locals come to relax.

items.activity: Find dinner — northern Thai food, yen ta fo, or market bites
items.note: If it's an evening-market day there's street food to graze on. Check the day before you go.

items.activity: Pick up any last souvenirs, then head back to your stay / back to Chiang Mai
items.note: The drive back to Chiang Mai takes about 40–50 min.

blocks.title: Doing Lamphun as a day trip from Chiang Mai
blocks.html: Plenty of people base themselves in Chiang Mai and drive over to Lamphun for a morning-to-evening day trip — it's only about 26 km. There's also a northern-line train; get off at Lamphun station, then walk or rent a vehicle into town. If you'd rather not rush, this one-day plan fits a morning-out, evening-back trip nicely.

blocks.text: Route and budget summary for one day

items: Morning — Wat Phra That Hariphunchai (free entry) + courtyard photos
Mid-morning — Hariphunchai Museum (~30 THB) + Wat Chamthewi / Ku Kut (free entry)
Lunch — northern Thai food: khao soi / khanom jeen nam ngiao / longan noodle soup
Afternoon — walk the old town + cafe + souvenirs (woven cloth / longan)
Overall budget per person — around 500–900 THB including food, museum entry, a cafe, and a few small souvenirs (not including vehicle rental)

blocks.html: All of this fits comfortably into one day. If you have more time, Lamphun also has the quiet, classic old town of Pa Sang, the Nong Ngueak weaving village, and Doi Khun Tan National Park to add on the next day.

faq.q: Is one day enough for Lamphun?
faq.a: It's enough for the main highlights — Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, the Hariphunchai museum, Wat Chamthewi, walking the old town, a cafe, and a northern Thai meal — because Lamphun is small and the sights are close together. If you order your stops well, you can see it all in a day without rushing.

faq.q: What are Wat Phra That Hariphunchai's hours, and is there an entry fee?
faq.a: It's open daily, roughly 06:00–21:00, and admission is free. It sits in the heart of Lamphun's old town. Mornings are best, with nice light and fewer people. Dress modestly and remove your shoes before entering the viharn.

faq.q: What days is the Hariphunchai museum open, and how much is entry?
faq.a: The Hariphunchai National Museum is open roughly 09:00–16:00, closed Monday–Tuesday and public holidays. Entry is around 30 THB for Thai visitors. It's diagonally opposite Wat Phra That Hariphunchai. If you come early in the week when it's closed, swap in the temple and old town instead.

faq.q: Do you need a private vehicle to visit Lamphun?
faq.a: Inside the old city walls you can walk to nearly everything. The only outlier is Wat Chamthewi, about 1.5 km outside town. For convenience, rent a motorbike for around 250–300 THB a day or borrow a bicycle from your guesthouse — Lamphun is an easy town to explore by bike.

faq.q: How do you get to Lamphun from Chiang Mai?
faq.a: Lamphun is only about 26 km from Chiang Mai. Driving takes around 40–50 minutes, or you can take the northern-line train to Lamphun station. Many people visit on a morning-out, evening-back day trip — and this one-day plan fits that day-trip pace from Chiang Mai perfectly.
